title: Finite algebraic axiomatization of full guarded KAT
formal: Does guarded Kleene algebra with tests admit a finite sound and complete algebraic calculus of the fixed-arity kind specified below for equality of guarded-string languages, uniformly over all finite sets of primitive actions and tests?
definitions:
Tests are Boolean terms in finitely many primitive tests, with 0,1,negation, conjunction and disjunction. Programs are primitive actions, tests used as assertions, sequential products ef, conditionals e+_b f (if b then e else f), and loops e^(b) (while b do e). An atom alpha is a complete truth assignment to primitive tests. A guarded string alternates atoms and actions, alpha_0 p_1 alpha_1 … p_n alpha_n, including a single atom when n=0. Fusion concatenates two strings only when the last atom of the first equals the first atom of the second, identifying that shared atom.

The language of b consists of atoms satisfying b; the language of an action p consists of all alpha p beta. Products use fusion. A conditional takes b-filtered traces of its first program and not-b-filtered traces of its second. A loop has language the union, for all j≥0, of j fused copies of b-filtered body traces followed by an atom satisfying not b. Thus only finite terminating traces count, and divergence contributes none. Language equality is literal equality of these sets.

Editorial calculus class: a fixed finite list of two-sorted equational axioms and quasi-equational rules, added to ordinary equational logic and Boolean algebra. Each rule is a fixed finite template of program/test equations as premises and one equation as conclusion, with universally substitutable program and test metavariables. It may also use the operation E from programs to tests, defined by E(b)=b, E(p)=0, E(ef)=E(e) and E(f), E(e+_b f)=(b and E(e)) or (not b and E(f)), and E(e^(b))=not b. These defining equations are available. No semantic side-condition, arbitrary list of metavariables, unbounded family of premises in one rule template, or auxiliary sort encoding derivations or automata is permitted. Every proof is finite. The calculus must be independent of the numbers of actions and tests. This specifies a finite algebraic basis question rather than the existence of any algorithmically checkable proof system.
answer_criterion: Exhibit such a finite calculus and prove in Lean that it derives exactly the language-valid program equations, or prove that no calculus in the stated class is complete. An equivalence algorithm alone does not provide a finite algebraic basis. Reusing an axiom scheme indexed by arbitrarily large equation systems does not satisfy the fixed-arity requirement.
context:
The GKAT axiomatization uses a uniqueness scheme for systems of equations with unbounded size. Although each instance is finite, the scheme is not a single fixed-arity rule of the class selected here.

The 2026 Hoare-hypothesis extension supplies additional completeness results while retaining the underlying GKAT axiomatization; it does not automatically remove that uniqueness scheme.
why: A finite axiomatization would give a compact proof theory for structured program equivalence.

import_provenance.original_title: A finite algebraic axiomatization of full guarded KAT
import_provenance.original_statement: Does full guarded Kleene algebra with tests admit a finite sound and complete algebraic inference system for its guarded-string language equivalence? In particular, determine whether the infinitary uniqueness axiom can be derived from the remaining finite axioms, rather than assuming a rule for arbitrary systems of equations.
